L004.summary: Erbach gives Ludwig VI eight reasons why he cannot leave his county: the troubled Empire, the electors' war nearby, his wife's illness, his brothers taking up government by connivance and a dispensation of age, their youthful counsels, his subjects' trust, the division of property, and disloyal councillors. He asks whether a lord may abandon church, subjects, house and wife and 'put his sheep under hirelings' (John 10:12). No. 2 (27 Apr 1666) refers to this letter of 'rationes', so it predates it.
L004.en:
[I have had to form] my thoughts about it, to disclose them obediently to Your Highness and to ask humbly for Your
Highness's understanding opinion. Your Highness will graciously remember that it was agreed between us that in this
matter each should speak and act according to his conscience. Accordingly I cannot refrain from saying it out, as I
ought: for the following reasons, however hard it is for me to bring myself to it, I have had to change the
resolution ...

First: the troubled state of public affairs stands in the way.
Second: the dangers from the electors' war, which is closest to me, and if armies and war parties pass over or
through it, of devastation.
Third: my wife's illness, growing daily.
Fourth and chiefly: my brother's government, which they are about to take up, partly by connivance, partly by a
dispensation of age.

L003.summary: Two short runs, 'unsers vorhabens' and 'mutationes', in a letter about a planned undertaking and the changes since.

L006.summary: 'Im Majo oder Junio will Gott unsere bonorum divisio vorgehen': the division of property with his brothers, point 7 of letter 004.

system: Letter-position book cipher (counted as homophonic): pair a,b is letter b of line a of a rhymed German Lord's Prayer of eight lines, so each letter has many cells.
